title: Leeman's research progress and his biography with Harlan Kenny
summary: After seven and a half hours of tapes Leeman takes a break to cook chowder, and says he has worked 80 to 90 hours on notes and is also working on a biography with Professor Harlan William Kenny.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I've been working on these last two and a half tapes, it looks like seven-and-a-half hours now, and I
don't want to get to the point where I was yesterday.

So, I believe I will take a rest now, and put on a pot for supper. I think maybe I'll make some potatoes and corn chowder that Charlie used to swap recipes with me, and I'll be thinking of him all the time I'm cooking.
I've put in almost five hours and more research in my musical career, and I'm getting to eliminate an awful lot of material that I consider most interesting, but we just don't have room for it.

I might say for the past two years, I've been working on my biography with Professor Dr. Harlan William Kenny, Professor of History at Kent State University in Ohio, and he has almost finished a biographical profile of me.

A lot of that research is helping me immensely on these tapes for the Smithsonian. I have all these tapes as reminders, and notes, rather, at hand. The profile isn't finished -- it's never been published, so it doesn't interfere with what we are doing.
There's so many musical events in my life, I've left information untouched. I'm sure a lot will be eliminated on the tapes, because as I said before, for want of time.

Well, I'm getting this project closer to a final summation of the work, so far -- I believe roughly on paper, I'm looking at it now -- I've been putting in around 80 to 90 hours this week; maybe I'll have a volume to equal
War and Peace before I'm through!
